truth: Niagara's generated property setters are one-argument slot writes (comp.setDouble(42.0), n.setBoolean(true)),
so a one-argument call is no write only for the bare name set (AtomicReference.set(v), ThreadLocal.set(v)): the
count exemption does not reach setDouble & co. A numeric first argument of set(0, v) (List.set) is no write either, and
comp.set("slot", v) with a slot name and a value is one. A.java holds the writes (a row per method: the call after x.set(v) is the write), B.java only calls that
are no component write (no rows, no no-csrf).

@DIR@/m
